key_insight: Removing viscous tilting of vorticity in DNS causes turbulence to change qualitatively, showing that viscous realignment is essential to Navier–Stokes turbulence structure.
engineering_relevance: The result highlights a non-negligible viscous mechanism that can alter cascade behavior and energy scaling, which matters for turbulence modeling and high-fidelity simulation design.
method: Ran direct numerical simulations of isotropic turbulence.
Surgically removed viscous tilting of vorticity from the governing dynamics.
Compared flow structure and energy spectra against standard Navier–Stokes turbulence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a drastic change in flow structure and a substantial deviation from the -5/3 inertial-range energy spectrum when viscous tilting is removed.
watch_item: This is a controlled numerical modification of the equations, so the effect may depend on the specific isotropic-turbulence setup and may not transfer directly to all wall-bounded or anisotropic flows.
paper_title: Turbulence Without the Viscous Tilting of Vorticity
